name: Wendy Haddad

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I’m with the independent Work Futures Panel. We have no ties to employers, AI companies, unions or government, and your answers are confidential. Tell me about a normal day at work.

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I’m 43, have an MBA, and lead seven buyers for a large pharmacy chain. We purchase medicines and basic supplies for many shops, and I spend mornings looking at what the stock system says will run out. I know which suppliers split an order and which shops have too little cold storage. I use an approved AI tool every day to compare demand and deliveries, but a pharmacist still has to tell me when a box arrived warm.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: Who depends on that wage at home?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: My husband teaches music at a school, and our children are seven and fifteen. We have a mortgage and nearly five months of expenses saved. My pay is normal for a manager at this level, and I could see a few other purchasing posts locally. I believe a business should keep its promises to customers and staff; a family cannot run on a slide deck about savings.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. "Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would say a small AI gain is welcome if it gives buyers more time to phone a pharmacy about missing stock. I would show the team how the tool counts unopened boxes, because a box in the system is no comfort when a patient cannot collect it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately I think I would remain in the job if AI Plateau is really mild. We have close to five months saved and two incomes, though our mortgage and the younger child’s after-school care still take steady wages. I like the tool, but I trust the pharmacist who opens the fridge.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This month I would keep our morning call with the three pharmacies that have the most missed deliveries. I would run the approved AI comparison alongside the stock ledger for a fortnight and ask the pharmacists to mark errors before changing an order. If the mild version settles in next year, I would keep that check and our ordinary savings transfer after the mortgage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel calm about my post in this version. I would be embarrassed if my tidy dashboard left a pharmacist apologising to a family.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What has the ledger missed?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A shipment showed as delivered to one pharmacy while its cold box was still on a van. The pharmacist could not dispense the medicine until its cold box was logged into the fridge. We held the next order until the box was logged into the fridge.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you expand the tool immediately?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Only after the two-week check shows which mistakes it makes. I use AI every day, but I have learned to keep the stock ledger beside it. Speed is useful only when we can find a missing medicine.

say: A **small AI gain** should free time to call pharmacies about stock.
I would show staff **unopened boxes** as well as system counts.
think: My **buyer post** looks steady under modest change.
The **mortgage and care bill** still need both wages despite five months saved.
do: **Keep** morning calls with three pharmacies about missed deliveries.
**Compare** approved AI counts with the stock ledger for two weeks before changing orders.
**Continue** the ordinary savings transfer after paying the mortgage.
feel: I feel **calm** about my post but embarrassed by screen errors at a pharmacy.
S0.quote: The pharmacist could not dispense the medicine until its cold box was logged into the fridge.
fieldNote: Her **daily AI use** already includes checking the stock ledger against real deliveries.
A **five-month reserve** and two wages support calm despite mortgage and after-school care.

steps.text: Keep morning calls with three pharmacies missing deliveries
Compare approved AI counts with stock ledger for two weeks before changing orders
Continue ordinary savings transfer after mortgage payment

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. "Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell my buyers that stronger AI may draft orders and compare supplier prices faster, and that could mean fewer buying posts. I would publish how many medicines actually reached a pharmacy, not just how many orders software raised. A company should pay for its mistakes instead of hiding them in a dashboard.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately I worry the company might merge buying teams and remove my seat despite my experience. I can learn new software quickly, but our mortgage does not care how adaptable I am. Five months saved would let us search, not make a lost salary harmless.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Next month I would run a four-week pilot that compares AI purchase suggestions with actual pharmacist stockouts, after the regional director approves it and gives my team paid time to check. I would ask the director to put the error and staffing figures in the same review. If the chain reduces buyers, I would apply to posted local supply-control jobs with pay after travel that covers our mortgage and with hours fitting the younger child’s care; I would accept only a confirmed offer after checking those terms.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about the buying team getting smaller. I am also keen to prove that an order raised is not the same as medicine available.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would count as a failed suggestion?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The tool proposed a cheaper supplier for a refrigerated medicine, but that supplier could deliver only on days the shop’s fridge was already full. The cheaper supplier’s box had nowhere safe to go in the pharmacy’s full fridge. A buyer had to call the pharmacist before approving it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Can you run the pilot on your own time?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No. The buyers already have a full order queue, and my youngest still needs after-school care. If the company wants a credible test, it must approve paid checking time rather than ask us to hide it after work.

say: **Buying automation** may shrink the team despite faster orders.
I would publish **pharmacy stockouts** beside the software’s savings.
think: My **manager seat** could vanish if buying teams merge.
Five months saved cannot replace a **lost salary** indefinitely.
do: **Run** a four-week purchase pilot only with director approval and paid team checking time.
**Report** stockout errors and staffing figures together.
**Apply** for posted supply-control jobs only with mortgage-covering net pay and childcare-compatible hours.
feel: I feel **anxious** about the team and eager to test actual availability.
S1.quote: The cheaper supplier’s box had nowhere safe to go in the pharmacy’s full fridge.
fieldNote: Her **daily tool use** drives a specific stockout pilot, conditional on paid checking time.
A **supply-control move** depends on an advertised vacancy and net pay that preserves mortgage and care.

steps.text: Run four-week AI order pilot only with director approval and paid team checking time
Report pharmacy stockouts and staffing alongside AI order savings
Apply to posted supply-control jobs only with mortgage-covering net pay and childcare-compatible hours
Accept confirmed offer only after checking net pay and family schedule

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. "Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the chain that AGI by 2028 could take buying plans and supplier negotiations before anyone has agreed who answers a pharmacist when a cold box fails. I would ask for a written staffing date and a route for a shop to override a wrong order.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately I fear our buying office could be cut quickly, and my job could go with it. Supply-control reports are thinking work as well and face 2028 AGI; physical shop and warehouse handling meets capable robots about 2031. We have nearly five months saved, which gives me choices, but a mortgage and care bill still require wages.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Next week I would ask the company’s staff forum for written severance and pharmacist-override terms. I would review our essential bills with my husband and apply for posted local pharmacy-operations work only if pay after travel covers the mortgage and after-school care. If AGI arrives in 2028 and my job ends, I would accept a role only after receiving an actual offer with those wages and a rota that lets one of us collect our nine-year-old.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious because the five-month buffer could vanish during a slow job search. I would rather name the risk now than tell my buyers an unposted job will save them.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would a pharmacist need to override?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: One pharmacy received a substitute medicine in the system before a pharmacist had approved its storage instructions. The pharmacist needs the power to hold the order, not just file a complaint after the box arrives. A patient can be left waiting while our buying office argues over who can hold a substitute medicine.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would the music-teaching wage cover you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My husband’s school pay helps, but it cannot cover the mortgage and care on its own. We would cut takeaway meals first if my pay stopped. I do not want to count his salary twice in a plan.

say: **2028 AGI** could remove buying plans before pharmacists gain override rights.
I would request written **staffing dates** and shop-order authority.
think: My **own job** could go as the buying office contracts.
Supply reports face **2028 AGI**, while physical handling robots arrive around 2031.
do: **Ask** the staff forum next week for severance and pharmacist-override terms.
**Review** essential bills with my husband and cut takeaway meals if my pay stops.
**Apply** for posted pharmacy-operations jobs with mortgage-and-care net pay; accept only an offer with pickup-fit rota.
feel: I feel **anxious** about a salary gap despite nearly five months saved.
S2.quote: A patient can be left waiting while our buying office argues over who can hold a substitute medicine.
fieldNote: Her **nearly five-month buffer** allows choices but cannot fund a long gap with mortgage and care.
She knows **operations paperwork** also faces 2028 AGI; handling robots follow around 2031.

steps.text: Ask staff forum for written severance and pharmacist-override terms
Cut takeaway meals if her buying salary stops
Apply for posted pharmacy-operations roles only with mortgage-and-care net pay
Accept confirmed offer only with pickup-compatible rota and verified net pay

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. "Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would say the extra years allow us to test a shop’s right to stop a bad order and to write down who must respond. By 2031 full AGI can still do buying and supply reports, so a new office title is not protection in itself.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately I could spend five years learning the actual cold-chain checks that happen between a van and a pharmacy fridge. The buying desk and the inspection report both face 2031 AGI, while physical handling meets capable robots about 2034. Our younger child will be twelve then, and my husband and I still need a workable rota and mortgage pay.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: From spring 2027 I would spend one paid day each month at a pharmacy recording arrival temperatures, only if the regional director approves buyer cover, my full salary continues and the pharmacist agrees to supervise. I would keep a log of where an AI order and an actual cold box disagree. After 2031 I would apply for an advertised cold-chain operations role only if it includes real authority to stop an unsafe delivery, net pay for our mortgage and a rota we can manage; I would take it only after a confirmed offer.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about the desk work, though a paid supervised day would show me whether I am suited to the shop side. I will not call a logbook a second career.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would the pharmacist supervise?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The thermometer reading, the seal and where the box went after unloading. I cannot learn a pharmacist’s cold-chain check by asking a chatbot to describe a fridge. The pharmacist has to show me when a batch must stay off the shelf.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why insist on full salary for a monthly visit?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The company benefits from finding spoiled stock before a customer does. My team still has purchase orders to finish and my household still has a mortgage. A visit squeezed into unpaid time would hide the cost of the experiment.

say: **2031 AGI** requires written shop-order authority, not a safer-sounding office title.
I would test **cold-chain checks** with real pharmacists.
think: Buying and inspection reports face **2031 AGI** before handling robots around 2034.
My **twelve-year-old** will still need a workable household rota.
do: **Visit** a pharmacy monthly from 2027 only with director-approved cover, full salary and pharmacist supervision.
**Log** mismatches between AI orders and cold-box temperatures.
**Apply** after 2031 only for advertised stop-delivery authority, mortgage-covering pay and a workable rota.
feel: I feel **anxious** about desk exposure but curious about supervised shop work.
S3.quote: I cannot learn a pharmacist’s cold-chain check by asking a chatbot to describe a fridge.
fieldNote: Her **monthly visit** is an approved paid test, not proof of a new position.
A **cold-chain role** needs advertised vacancy, stop-delivery authority, sufficient net pay and a family rota.

steps.text: Visit pharmacy monthly only with director-approved cover full salary and pharmacist supervision
Log AI-order and cold-box mismatches during approved visits
Apply for advertised cold-chain role only with stop-delivery authority mortgage pay and family rota
Take role only after confirmed offer with those pay and authority terms

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. "Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell colleagues a decade gives the chain time to put shop override rights into contracts and to show staff the pay of new roles. I would not call a patient’s missed medicine a good saving simply because the purchase price fell.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately our mortgage might be lower by 2036, and our children will be seventeen and twenty-five. I cannot assume any buying or operations report survives 2036 AGI; robots doing physical handling arrive about 2039. I have time to strengthen our cash buffer and understand shop operations, but neither guarantees a vacancy.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I would keep daily stock calls and add seventy to savings only in months when both wages arrive, the mortgage and care bills clear and there is no school trip cost. I would ask the regional director to make pharmacist stop-order rights part of the next contract revision. After 2036 I would stay in pharmacy operations only while I can actually hold an unsafe delivery and the job pays our bills; if either condition fails I would search posted roles locally.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel uneasy about treating a decade as a promise. I can improve the current contract and cash reserve without pretending I know the 2036 job list.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why cash rather than an extra mortgage payment?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A mortgage overpayment would lock the money away. We have almost five months saved, but a job search could take longer than that. The extra seventy would come only from a full-pay month after the household costs.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Does the younger child still need pickup in 2036?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: At seventeen, the child will not need the same after-school collection. We will have a different family timetable then. I still would not accept a wage that leaves the mortgage unpaid.

say: A **decade** should bring written shop override rights and published role pay.
I would reject **cheap purchases** that leave patients without medicine.
think: Both children will be older and the **mortgage** may shrink by 2036.
Buying reports face **2036 AGI**, with physical handling robots around 2039.
do: **Save** seventy extra only after both wages, mortgage and care bills clear, with no school trip cost.
**Ask** for stop-order rights in the next contract; stay after 2036 only with real authority and bill-paying wages.
feel: I feel **uneasy** about the distant job list but able to improve today’s contract.
S4.quote: A mortgage overpayment would lock the money away.
fieldNote: Her **extra cash** comes from earnings only after full wages, household bills and no school trip cost.
The **seventeen-year-old** no longer needs 2026 pickup arrangements by 2036.

steps.text: Keep daily calls with pharmacies about missing stock
Save seventy only after both wages mortgage care paid and no school trip cost
Search posted local roles if post-2036 operations loses authority or bill-paying wages

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most, because the buying office could contract before pharmacists have the right to stop a wrong order. I would need written staffing terms and a genuine override route, plus enough paid time to test cold-chain work while I still have a salary. My husband’s wage cannot carry the mortgage alone.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: Ask the pharmacist whether a medicine actually reached the fridge. A purchase order is not a box a patient can collect. The person standing at the counter must be able to tell my office we got it wrong.

headlineQuote: A purchase order is not a box a patient can collect.
portrait: **Wendy, 43**, is an MBA-trained senior buyer managing seven staff for a large pharmacy chain.
Her **typical pay**, music-teacher husband, nearly five-month reserve and some local posts support a mortgage and two children.
She uses **AI daily** to compare demand and deliveries, while pharmacists verify cold boxes.
She is **calm** with mild change, anxious about quick office cuts and tests paid shop visits before any move.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could cut her buying post before pharmacists have real override authority.
whatWouldHelp: Written **staffing terms**, shop overrides and paid supervised cold-chain tests would help.
